stem: A developer on the Open Plan submits jobs to a real QPU inside `Session(backend=backend)`. What happens, and what should they do instead?

options.text: The session opens normally — on the free Open Plan all three execution modes accept jobs.
Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs; job mode or batch mode is the recommended path.
Sessions work on the Open Plan but are limited to a single job each.
The Open Plan supports sessions but not batch mode.
The session opens, but the Open Plan caps it at a 10-minute maximum TTL, after which queued jobs fail.
Session and batch both need a paid plan; the Open Plan generally supports job mode only.

explanation.correct: The documentation states explicitly that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs; their workloads must run in job mode or batch mode. Sessions (dedicated, exclusive access) are reserved for paid plans.

distractors.A: The Open Plan does NOT accept session jobs; only job mode and batch mode are available to it.
distractors.C: Sessions are not merely limited on the Open Plan — they cannot be submitted at all.
distractors.D: It is the reverse: batch mode IS available on the Open Plan (with a 10-minute max TTL); sessions are not.
distractors.E: The 10-minute maximum TTL is the Open Plan default for BATCH mode, from the batch guide's TTL table. Sessions get no Open Plan limit because Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs at all.
distractors.F: This over-corrects: batch mode IS available on the Open Plan. Only session jobs are restricted, which is why the documented advice for Open Plan users is job mode or batch mode.
